<p class="sardine-eyebrow">DERAILED / MARINE LIFE / EXPERIMENT NO. 016</p>

# First, make a sardine.

<p class="sardine-lede">At Aquamarine Fukushima, thousands of Japanese sardines moved together like one enormous creature. Before trying to explain a school, let's build just one fish.</p>

<div class="sardine-intro">ONE FISH → MOVEMENT → A SCHOOL</div>

```{=html}
<section class="sardine-lab" aria-label="Interactive sardine generator">
  <div class="lab-heading">
    <div><span class="lab-kicker">01 / A LITTLE FISH FACTORY</span><h2>Meet your sardine.</h2></div>
    <div class="lab-state" id="fish-status" role="status" aria-live="polite">One fish, no leader.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="tank-shell">
    <canvas id="sardine-canvas" aria-label="Animated silver sardine swimming in a blue aquarium" role="img"></canvas>
    <div class="tank-caption"><span>THE TANK / LIVE SIMULATION</span><span id="fish-count-label">1 SARDINE</span></div>
  </div>
  <div class="lab-controls">
    <div class="sliders">
      <label for="fish-length">Body length <output id="length-value">120</output><input id="fish-length" type="range" min="65" max="180" value="120" step="1"></label>
      <label for="fish-depth">Body depth <output id="depth-value">32</output><input id="fish-depth" type="range" min="16" max="55" value="32" step="1"></label>
      <label for="fish-speed">Swim speed <output id="speed-value">1.0</output><input id="fish-speed" type="range" min="0" max="3" value="1" step="0.1"></label>
    </div>

  </div>
  <p class="lab-note">Try changing its proportions. The fish is drawn using JavaScript Canvas paths—not an image file. Speed affects how fast it swims; the tail swishes even when the fish is staying in place.</p>
</section>
```

## 02 / A tiny set of instructions

This sardine has a body shape and a little state: its position, direction, speed, and tail phase. On every animation frame we update that state and draw it again.

The first experiment deliberately contains **one** fish. We can understand its shape and motion before adding interactions with neighbours.

## 03 / What if there were hundreds?

That is the next detour: **separation** (don't crowd), **alignment** (head the same way), and **cohesion** (stay near neighbours). Together, those local rules form a simplified model called *Boids*. They help us explore emergence, but they are not a complete explanation of real sardine behaviour.

<p class="sardine-outro">The first question isn't “Who leads the school?” It's “What does each fish do?”</p>
